Propose foreign key relationships from the column profile

Source: R/foreign_keys.R
infer_foreign_keys.Rd

Tier-one inference, from profile statistics alone and without extra queries. Every column of a string, integer or uuid type is scored against every pk_candidate column in another table (or another column of the same table), and the best-scoring target at or above min_confidence is recorded. These are candidates only: a shortlist for the key register's match-rate tests, which are the only thing that can confirm a relationship.

Usage

infer_foreign_keys(profile, min_confidence = 0.6)

Arguments

profile

A column_profile from db_profile(), ideally covering every table of interest: a key in a table that is not in profile cannot be proposed.

min_confidence

Lowest score that counts as a candidate.

Value

profile with fk_candidate (logical), fk_target (schema.table.column of the best key, or NA), fk_confidence, fk_evidence (the scoring components as text) and fk_n_targets added or replaced.

Exclusions

A pair is ruled out, whatever else it scores, when:

  • the type classes differ, or the child's string lengths fall outside the key's;

  • the child is itself unique and shares the key's value_fingerprint: that is a copy of the key, which belongs in the duplicate map;

  • the key's complete value set is known (its distinct count is within the values recorded for it) and a top value of the child is not in it;

  • the key's table was profiled in full and the child has more distinct values than the key;

  • the shapes of the two columns' top values (runs of digits, letters and other characters) do not overlap, so 100 cannot reference Ward 3;

  • the child is a flag, or is empty;

  • the key is in the child's own table and the names do not say it is a self-reference (exact or suffix match);

  • the child is itself a pk_candidate and there is no name evidence: a key that merely resembles another key is a coincidence or a copy.

Scoring

Surviving pairs start at 0.1 and add:

  • name evidence: 0.45 for the same normalised name, 0.3 when the child name ends with the key name (prior_mrn to mrn), 0.2 when it contains the key's table stem (main_site to sites.site_code). Generic column names such as id, code, name or description earn nothing on their own; their keys are reached through the table stem;

  • values: when the key's complete value set is known and every top value of the child is in it, 0.4 times the share of the key's values the child uses, so a child that uses all of a code list scores more than one that uses two of its seven codes;

  • range: when the value set is not known but both ranges are, 0.25 if the child's min and max lie inside the key's and -0.25 if they do not;

  • cardinality, when the key's table was profiled in full: 0.15 for a many-to-one shape, 0.05 for one-to-one unless the child is itself a pk_candidate;

  • 0.1 when both columns have the same minimum and maximum string length, unless the child is itself a pk_candidate.

Scores are capped at 1. Ties go to the key with the fewest distinct values when membership is known (the tightest fit) and the most when it is not (a table rather than a view of it), then by name. fk_n_targets counts how many keys reached the threshold, since a conformed code such as a site code legitimately matches several.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- fakehospdata::fh_connect("sample")
inv <- db_inventory(con, include = c("pas_patients$", "pas_adt_events$"), progress = FALSE)
prof <- db_profile(con, inv, progress = FALSE)
prof[prof$fk_candidate, c("table_name", "column_name", "fk_target", "fk_confidence")]
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
} # }
